scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

The decision to take a prestigious job offer in a new city or stay in a modest role to remain close to family is a deeply personal one, and there's no one-size-fits-all answer. However, I can provide some factors to consider that might have helped inform your decision: **Pros of taking the prestigious job offer:** 1. **Career advancement**: A prestigious job can bring new challenges, opportunities for growth, and a significant boost to your career. 2. **Personal development**: Living in a new city can be a transformative experience, allowing you to develop new skills, meet new people, and broaden your perspectives. 3. **Financial benefits**: A higher salary and better benefits can improve your financial stability and security. **Cons of taking the prestigious job offer:** 1. **Family separation**: Leaving your family behind can be emotionally challenging, especially if you have close relationships with them. 2. **Uncertainty**: Adapting to a new city, job, and environment can be stressful and uncertain. 3. **Support system**: You may need to rebuild your support network, which can take time. **Pros of staying in the modest role:** 1. **Family proximity**: Remaining close to your family can provide emotional support, comfort, and a sense of belonging. 2. **Familiarity**: Staying in a familiar environment can reduce stress and uncertainty. 3. **Community ties**: You may have established a strong network of friends, colleagues, and community connections. **Cons of staying in the modest role:** 1. **Limited career growth**: Staying in a modest role may limit your career advancement opportunities and potential. 2. **Stagnation**: You may feel like you're not challenging yourself or growing professionally. 3. **Regret**: You might wonder what could have been if you had taken the prestigious job offer. Ultimately, the decision depends on your personal priorities, values, and goals. If you value career advancement, personal growth, and financial security, taking the prestigious job offer might have been the better choice. However, if family and community ties are essential to your well-being, staying in the modest role could have been the more suitable option. As you've already made your decision, I'm curious – what did you end up choosing, and how are you feeling about your decision now?
